clue.text: Sad dark sorrow? One right to leave a necessary nuisance

indicators.note: something sad is in a sorry, disordered state, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the letter for 'one right' departs from the fodder before the rest is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a single R, the abbreviation for right, which is removed

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about grief, followed by someone walking off from a necessary evil.
explanation.walkthrough: DARK SORROW has three Rs; drop one and the remaining nine letters rearrange. 'Sad' at the front looks like part of the picture of grief but is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to the road are an irritating delay for drivers, yet they have to be done, hence a necessary nuisance.

clue.text: Puzzle concerning coach

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
a coach is a kind of bus

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a coach, perhaps a sports trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle where images and letters stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Harmony blokes found in a welcome

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: things found in something sit inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to greet someone is to welcome them
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: A group of friendly chaps greeting each other in perfect accord.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement and harmony are both states where people are in accord rather than in conflict.

clue.text: Wide blighter that's backing bill — one's full of rubbish

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a heel is a contemptible person, a rotter
i.e., id est, means that is

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word for bill is read from end to start

parts.note: a bird's bill or beak is also called its nib

explanation.surface: A dodgy person supporting a piece of legislation is dismissed as talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheelie bin is the British household rubbish bin on wheels. 'Full of rubbish' sounds like an insult about the blighter but is literally true of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled dustbin is a container stuffed with household waste, so it is literally full of garbage.

clue.text: Stays on channels

parts.note: re means on or about
side is old British slang for a TV channel, as in 'switch to the other side'

explanation.surface: Someone keeps watching the same TV channels.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live or remain there, so the verb matches 'stays' in the sense of dwelling.

clue.text: Such as point to groups of deplorables?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who show or point things out
second meaning: a shower is British slang for a useless or contemptible bunch of people

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the answer as SHOW-ERS, people who show; the second is the British put-down 'what a shower', meaning a bad lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who indicate or display are literally ones who show; and a shower in British slang is a disreputable crowd.

clue.text: Exhausted from endless ringing

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are lopped off the word

parts.note: ringing someone is calling them on the phone

explanation.surface: Someone worn out by a phone or bell that will not stop.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is an informal idiom meaning completely tired out.

clue.text: Drink that seen in the course of Christmas time

indicators.note: something occurring in the course of a phrase lies within its run of letters

parts.note: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: A drink spotted being poured over the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the break between chriSTMAS and TIme.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is a drink.

clue.text: This could be filthy and it could also be cruel

definitions.note: the definition is the familiar phrase 'filthy lucre', with the answer the noun it describes

indicators.note: saying the letters could also form something signals that they may be shuffled into another word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something described as both dirty and unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the stock phrase 'filthy lucre', meaning money gained dishonourably.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre means money or profit, and the fixed idiom 'filthy lucre' makes it the thing that could be filthy.

clue.text: Jonquil who only contemplates himself?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the jonquil is a species of this flower genus
second meaning: the youth of Greek myth who fell in love with his own reflection

explanation.walkthrough: In myth the beautiful youth pined away gazing at himself in a pool and became the flower, which ties the two senses together.
explanation.definitionFit: The jonquil belongs to the daffodil genus of that name, and the mythical figure is the archetype of self-absorption.

clue.text: Lighter but for half of gear

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

indicators.note: taking half of a word keeps only its first two of four letters

parts.note: the front half of the word

explanation.surface: Something would weigh less were it not for half the equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is the noun for a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed boat used to ferry cargo to and from ships, a kind of barge.

clue.text: E-type perhaps shown by blemish after use in public

indicators.note: one thing coming after another puts it second in the line-up

parts.note: to sport something is to wear or display it openly
a scar is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: A car showing a scratch after it has been out on the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: The E-type is the classic 1960s Jaguar; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jaguar E-type is a famous example of a fast two-seater built for performance.

clue.text: One gets you up to walk then run

parts.note: to step is to walk
a ladder is a run in tights or stockings; 'then' places it second

explanation.surface: Advice for a morning routine: something to get you going, first walking then running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets you up' sounds like waking someone, but it means raising you physically.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding set of steps lets you climb up to reach somewhere high.

clue.text: Headgear mostly cared for by one

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: something cared for is kept, as animals are kept
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hat that someone has mostly looked after themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A kepi is a French military cap with a flat circular top and a peak.

clue.text: Idiots grip part of transmission

parts.note: cranks are eccentric or foolish people
a haft is the handle or grip of a tool or weapon

explanation.surface: Foolish people get hold of part of a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transmission' suggests broadcasting, but it is a vehicle's drive train.
explanation.definitionFit: The crankshaft turns the pistons' motion into rotation, a key component of an engine's power train.

clue.text: Exams could be smooth since outside

indicators.note: one word standing outside another wraps around it

parts.note: as means since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'
to level a surface is to make it smooth and flat

explanation.surface: Tests might go easily because of where they are held.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels are the advanced exams English and Welsh pupils take at about 18 for university entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced-level school-leaving qualifications in Britain are a set of examinations.

clue.text: Echoing round sound of bells is attractive

indicators.note: an echo repeats what is heard, so the phrase is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: a peal is a round of bells rung in sequence

explanation.surface: The chime of church bells ringing round is a pleasing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a pealing' is indistinguishable from the adjective meaning attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing draws you in, the same as being attractive or pleasing.

clue.text: Better gent heard to be successful

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken aloud, so the word for gent counts by its sound

parts.note: sir is the polite address for a gentleman
to pass a test is to succeed in it

explanation.surface: A gentleman is rumoured to have done better than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective but is the verb meaning outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to exceed or outdo them, the verb sense of better.

clue.text: A poet, I pen vibrantly for someone who's posted

indicators.note: vibrant writing is full of lively movement, so the letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet boasts of writing lively verse for a correspondent who has been sent a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' looks like letters in the mail, but it means assigned to a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone posted to a role has been appointed to it, so they are an appointee.

clue.text: Loyal devotee of mass involving Trinity

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pat is a small mass, as in a pat of butter
a trinity is a group of three

explanation.surface: A faithful churchgoer who attends a Mass celebrating the Holy Trinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service, but here it is a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone loyally devoted to their country.

clue.text: Huge drop of colour on refurbished Titian

indicators.note: something refurbished has been done over and rearranged, so the letters are reordered
just a drop is the smallest amount, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A restored Titian painting gains a tiny dab of fresh paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter, which suits the art-restoration picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means of enormous size or strength, after the giant Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Drop parrot's nibbles

parts.note: to can something is informally to drop or scrap it
parrot's read as parrot is: to parrot is to imitate, and so is to ape

explanation.surface: A pet bird's snacks being dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', and the verb sense of parrot is needed; 'nibbles' is the noun for party snacks, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapés are small savoury bites served with drinks, the kind of snacks called nibbles.

clue.text: Foreign estate prattle over Perrier, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece being over another places it first, on top

parts.note: to chat is to talk idly
Perrier is a French mineral water, and eau is French for water

explanation.surface: Chatter about a bottle of Perrier at an overseas property.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French country house with its estate, often a wine-producing property.

clue.text: A stroke of satire that doesn't quite finish sadly

indicators.note: not quite finishing means stopping one letter short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
a lash is a stroke of a whip, and a cutting remark in satire

explanation.surface: A satirical jab that falls flat at the end, which is a pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection expressing grief or regret, used like 'unfortunately' or sadly.

clue.text: Priest relinquishing power would be a burning issue

indicators.note: relinquishing means giving something up, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A clergyman giving up authority would be a hotly debated topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning issue' normally means an urgent topic; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, literally a matter of burning.

clue.text: 18 and the like in a healthy way cooks joints

parts.note: steaming is a healthy way of cooking
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: Someone cooking meat joints healthily, alongside a cross-reference to another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is TITANIC, the steam-driven liner; 'joints' suggests roasts of meat but means body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was a steam-powered ocean liner, so it and similar vessels are examples of this class of ship.

clue.text: Plunders old white wines

definitions.meaning: first meaning: loots, as an army does to a captured town
second meaning: sack was an old name for dry white wines from Spain and the Canaries

explanation.walkthrough: Sack is the fortified wine Falstaff loves in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a city is to pillage it; and sack was the historical term for sherry-like white wines imported from Spain.

clue.text: God of aerospace?

indicators.note: letters of a word are part of it, so the answer is found inside the next word

parts.note: the letters sit within the word

explanation.surface: A playful question asking who the deity of flight technology would be.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies in aEROSpace; the winged god fits the idea of flight, which is why the clue has a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek deity of love, a winged figure equivalent to Cupid.

clue.text: Security given by a type of hedge?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a hedge in finance is a protective bet, and the question mark flags the leafy garden reading as false

explanation.surface: Privacy and safety provided by a particular variety of garden hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hedge' pictures a garden boundary, but it is the financial sense, as in hedging against risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy protecting against loss gives financial security, and hedging one's bets is a form of protecting against loss.

clue.text: French will abandon desperate stunt

indicators.note: abandoning something means leaving it behind, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: frantic means desperate, out of control with worry
FR is the abbreviation for French

explanation.surface: The French will give up a reckless act.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a silly or grotesque caper, a playful trick like a stunt.

clue.text: One'll leave expert group

indicators.note: to leave is to depart, so a letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a genius is a highly gifted expert
one is the Roman numeral I; the contracted 'will' only makes the instruction a sentence

explanation.surface: A specialist is departing from a team.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'one will leave expert': the numeral comes out of the word for an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classification rank grouping closely related species.

clue.text: Legion to matter not so much

parts.note: to count is to matter, as in 'every vote counts'
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A Roman army unit mattering less than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' looks like a noun for soldiers, but it is the adjective meaning very many, as in 'their fans are legion'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a predicate adjective legion means numerous beyond reckoning, too many to be totted up.
